message.content:
Copenhagen is an igneous stone other than granite, worked and polished into slabs. That points to heading 6802, which covers worked monumental or building stone. Subheading 6802.93 covers granite, and 6802.99 covers other stone. Because the lab found an "other igneous stone" rather than granite, it falls under 6802.99.

I considered 6802.91 (marble, travertine, alabaster) and 6802.92 (other calcareous stone), but neither fits an igneous stone. Within 6802.99, the statistical suffixes are 6802.99.0010 for slate and 6802.99.0090 for other. The other-igneous classification therefore lands in 6802.99.0090.

Heading 6802 also has a subheading for stone "further worked than simply cut or sawn", and a polished surface counts as further worked. The 6802.99.00 line is the one for "other stone: other," and I am recalling that the HTS splits it into 6802.99.0010 (calcareous stone, other than marble/travertine/alabaster) and 6802.99.0090 (other). Since this stone is igneous, the 6802.99.0090 line is the one that applies.

{"hts_code": "6802.99.0090", "reason": "Polished slabs of an igneous stone other than granite, for countertops and flooring, are worked building stone of heading 6802, falling under the 'other stone, other' subheading."}
